speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin; tell me, how many days old are you, and has your urine or stool turned white or clay-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: That's a 2-week-old female, exclusively breastfed, with worsening jaundice over the last two days. Given her age and weight gain, I need to rule out biliary atresia; can you tell me if her stool has ever been clay-colored? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_fractionation (Direct/Indirect).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Indirect: 15.4 mg/dL

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born at 39 weeks' gestation. Exclusive breastfeeding. Family history notable for older brother's death possibly related to liver issues. Social history: Not applicable for age.

speaker: Patient
text: Temperature of 37.1°C, pulse of 145/min, and respirations of 40/min. No other symptoms reported by the caregiver. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The vital signs appear stable; however, to distinguish between physiological jaundice and biliary atresia, I need to see the direct bilirubin levels. REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_fractionation (Direct/Indirect). Please also send me any images of her stool color.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Indirect: 15.4 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Late-Onset Physiological Jaundice). The fractionated bilirubin shows a predominantly indirect pattern (Direct 0.7 mg/dL) with a total level of 16.1 mg/dL, which rules out biliary atresia and cholestasis. Please continue exclusive breastfeeding to maintain hydration and promote bilirubin excretion.
